newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's hard left says will reject Albania motion.
newsitem.headline: Italy's hard left says will reject Albania motion.

text.p: The Communist Refoundation party confirmed on Wednesday it would vote against a government motion on the deployment of Italian troops to Albania, despite a last minute appeal for support from Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Prodi told the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) that he would put the fate of his government in the hands of President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro if his hard left ally, which holds the balance of the power in the Chamber, voted against the motion.

But the chairman of Communist Refoundation, Armando Cossutta, told reporters his party would continue to oppose the Italian-led multinational operation in Albania. "On Albania we will vote 'no,' as we have already stated," Cossutta said.

The vote in the lower chamber is due around 8.00 p.m. (1800 GMT). Prodi's centre-left coalition cannot win the motion without Refoundation support, unless the centre-right opposition bloc throws its weight behind the government.

Prodi appealed in his speech to all parties to back the government motion. If he turns to Scalfaro, the president would have several options available. He could ask Prodi to offer his resignation or send him to parliament for a confidence vote.

Refoundation has said it would back the government in a confidence test as long as it was not on Albania. "We are against the Albania expedition but we are not against the government," Cossutta said. "We must wait to see how the government will propose its confidence motion," he added.
